summary: Backend-only testing for Portal Orang Tua Asuh. Created /app/backend/tests/backend_test.py with 21 pytest tests covering auth, dashboard, guardians (CRUD, portal token uniqueness/regeneration), children (CRUD + unique NIM), photo upload+download, relations (create/duplicate/delete), donations (guardian-only, no child_id), developments, reports (upsert + monthly merge with all guardians), public portal (no auth, no per-child donation attribution, 404 on invalid token), and settings. All 21 tests pass (100%).

minor.issue: Enforces -n 2 --dist loadscope; class-scoped shared TEST_STATE breaks under loadscope because sibling classes get split across workers. Tests are stable only with -n 0. Command to run: `pytest backend/tests/backend_test.py -n 0`.

allow_credentials=False while login sets an httpOnly cookie with SameSite=None Secure — cookie-based auth from browser will not send credentials cross-site. Frontend must therefore rely on Authorization: Bearer header (which it does via localStorage token). Not blocking, but the cookie is effectively dead-weight in this config.
No brute-force lockout / rate limit implemented (playbook mentions 5-fail lockout). Not enforced by request but worth noting.

action_items: Optional: relax pytest.ini or make tests self-contained per-test if parallel execution is desired.
Optional: add brute-force lockout on /api/auth/login per playbook guidance.
Optional: fix CORS/cookie mismatch (allow_credentials=True + explicit origins) if cookie-based session is intended; otherwise remove the cookie set as it currently serves no purpose.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py is 980 lines — consider splitting into routers/models/seed modules (>700 line guideline).
CORS allow_origins=['*'] with allow_credentials=False is inconsistent with cookie-based auth attempt; either enable credentials with explicit origin list, or drop the cookie.
put_object/get_object are synchronous requests inside async endpoints — will block the event loop under load; consider httpx.AsyncClient or run_in_threadpool.
No rate limiting / lockout on login endpoint.
MongoDB unique index on relations (guardian_id, child_id) is created on startup — good; app-level duplicate check exists — good.
Public portal correctly omits child_id/guardian_id/child_name from donations (verified by test).
Regenerate-token endpoint correctly invalidates the old token (verified: old token → 404, new → 200).
seed_data_creation: Startup seed already creates 5 guardians, 10 children, 15 donations, ~30 developments, and reports for 2026-06/2026-07/2026-08. Tests create TEST_-prefixed guardians/children which are cleaned up by test_zzz_cleanup.
